# @cubicecho/agent-mcp-pool

> A pool of long-lived Model Context Protocol clients, exposing every connected server's tools to an OpenAI-compatible agent loop as `<slug>__<tool>`.

What is here is connection management: reconciling configured servers against the clients actually running, naming their tools so a model can call them, and refusing a call to a server the run was not scoped to. Where the configuration comes from is the caller's — see `McpPoolOptions.load`.

Requires Node >=22, with `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` >=1.30 as peer dependency. ESM only.
Full prose, worked examples and the reasoning behind each seam are in README.md; this file is the index.

## Exports

### @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js

- `CallToolResult` (type)
- `ElicitRequestParams` (type)
- `ElicitResult` (type)
- `Notification` (type)
- `ServerCapabilities` (type)
- `ToolAnnotations` (type)

### arguments

Arguments as a model wrote them, brought into line with the schema the server published.

- `CoercedArguments` (type) — What `coerceArguments` returns.
- `coerceArguments` — Repairs a model's arguments against a tool's input schema, and says what it could not repair.

### errors

- `httpStatusFor` — The HTTP status a gateway answers each refusal with.
- `McpPoolError` — A refusal from the pool, with a discriminant.
- `McpPoolErrorCode` (type) — Which of the pool's refusals this is.
- `McpPoolErrorOptions` (type) — What an `McpPoolError` carries beyond its message.

### hooks

MCP tools as lifecycle hooks — the half that needs no connection.

- `ContextBlocks` (type) — What `contextBlocks` built, and what each hook contributed to it.
- `contextBlocks` — The injecting hooks' output, as context for the model.
- `DEFAULT_HOOK_MAX_TOKENS` — The cap on one hook's injected text when its row does not set `maxTokens`.
- `ExpandedArgs` (type) — What `expandArgs` made of a hook's arguments.
- `expandArgs` — Fills a hook's `args` from its context.
- `HOOK_EVENTS` — Every event a hook can be bound to, in the order a session meets them.
- `hookVars` — The template paths an event offers, `vars.*` aside.
- `INJECT_EVENTS` — The events whose output can reach the model.
- `INJECT_TIMEOUT_MS` — How long a hook something waits on gets when its row does not say.
- `readVeto` — Whether a hook's answer asked for a veto, and why.
- `templatePaths` — Every path a hook's `args` names, each once.
- `VETO_EVENTS` — The events a hook may decline.
- `validateHooks` — What is wrong with a row's hooks, for the form that saves them.

### listing

- `listAllTools` — Every tool a server offers, following `tools/list`'s cursor to the end.

### pool

- `CallOptions` (type) — How one `call()` is made, beyond its name and arguments.
- `DescribeOptions` (type) — What `describe()` takes beside the name.
- `McpPool` — One MCP client per configured server, exposing their tools to an agent loop as `<slug>__<tool name>`.
- `McpPoolOptions` (type) — How a pool is built: where its rows come from, how patient it is, and what it may spawn.
- `PoolLog` (type) — Where the pool's own progress goes.
- `RunHooksOptions` (type) — What `runHooks` takes beyond the event and its context.
- `StateOptions` (type) — What `state()` takes: whether the rows it reports come back with their credentials.
- `ToolsOptions` (type) — What `tools()` takes: which tools to send, and which servers this run may reach.

### probe

- `ProbeOptions` (type) — What a probe takes from the caller: the child's environment, and its patience.
- `probe` — Connects to a config that may not be saved yet, lists its tools, and hangs up.

### results

- `resultText` — What a tool call is worth as a tool message.
- `truncateText` — Text cut to fit a character budget, keeping its head and its tail.

### servers

Questions about server rows that need neither a connection nor Node — for the form that edits one.

- `fromMcpServersJson` — Rows from the `mcpServers` JSON that Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and most server READMEs describe a server with.
- `McpServersJsonOptions` (type) — What `fromMcpServersJson` needs besides the JSON.
- `sameConnection` — Whether two rows describe the same live connection.
- `serversWith` — The connected servers that offer a capability — the filter every host wrote for itself.
- `validateServerConfig` — What is wrong with a row, for the form that saves it — before `sync()` is handed it.

### transport

- `createTransport` — The transport a config asks for, stdio or streamable HTTP, ready to connect.
- `MINIMAL_CHILD_ENV` — A short allowlist of variables a stdio child usually cannot start without.
- `readStderrTail` — Starts collecting a stdio child's stderr, and returns a reader for the last of it.
- `TransportFactory` (type) — What builds the transport for one connection, where the pool's own construction is not wanted.
- `TransportOptions` (type) — What a transport takes beyond the config itself.

### types

- `CatalogServer` (type) — One server's tools, without their JSON schemas — the cheap half of a tool definition.
- `ClientIdentity` (type) — How this process introduces itself in a handshake: the `clientInfo` of MCP's `initialize`.
- `HookContext` (type) — What a host knows at an event, for a hook's templates.
- `HookEvent` (type) — A point in a session a hook can be bound to.
- `HookMessage` (type) — One message of a session as a hook is handed it.
- `HookOutcome` (type) — What one hook did.
- `HttpServerConfig` (type) — A server reached over streamable HTTP, at a url this process does not own the lifetime of.
- `McpConnection` (type) — What it takes to reach a server — the connection half of a row, without its identity.
- `McpProbe` (type) — What `probe` found: whether the config works, and what it offers if it does.
- `McpServerConfig` (type) — A configured MCP server, as this package needs it.
- `McpServerPublicConfig` (type) — A row as `state()` reports it: everything except the credentials, unless they were asked for.
- `McpServerState` (type) — One connected server as an operator sees it.
- `McpStatus` (type) — `idle` is registered-but-not-connected, and where an idle-reaped server goes — a success state: nothing is wrong, there is simply no child right now.
- `PoolCloseReason` (type) — Why a connection closed, on a `close` event.
- `PoolEvent` (type) — Something the pool did, as `McpPool.onEvent` reports it.
- `StdioServerConfig` (type) — A server reached by spawning a child process and speaking MCP over its stdio.
- `ToolDefinition` (type) — One tool as an OpenAI-compatible model is offered it — the function arm of OpenAI's `ChatCompletionTool`, and assignable to it.
- `ToolHook` (type) — One tool call a row wants made at a point in a session.
- `ToolInfo` (type) — One tool in full, as `McpPool.describe` returns it: what `ToolDefinition` has no room for.

## Subpath entries

### @cubicecho/agent-mcp-pool/hooks

MCP tools as lifecycle hooks — the half that needs no connection.

Importable in a browser as `@cubicecho/agent-mcp-pool/hooks`, for the editor that saves a row's hooks: nothing here, and nothing it imports, reaches for a `node:` module or the SDK at runtime.

- `HOOK_EVENTS` — Every event a hook can be bound to, in the order a session meets them.
- `INJECT_EVENTS` — The events whose output can reach the model.
- `VETO_EVENTS` — The events a hook may decline.
- `INJECT_TIMEOUT_MS` — How long a hook something waits on gets when its row does not say.
- `DEFAULT_HOOK_MAX_TOKENS` — The cap on one hook's injected text when its row does not set `maxTokens`.
- `hookVars` — The template paths an event offers, `vars.*` aside.
- `templatePaths` — Every path a hook's `args` names, each once.
- `ExpandedArgs` (type) — What `expandArgs` made of a hook's arguments.
- `expandArgs` — Fills a hook's `args` from its context.
- `validateHooks` — What is wrong with a row's hooks, for the form that saves them.
- `readVeto` — Whether a hook's answer asked for a veto, and why.
- `ContextBlocks` (type) — What `contextBlocks` built, and what each hook contributed to it.
- `contextBlocks` — The injecting hooks' output, as context for the model.
- `HookContext` (type)
- `HookEvent` (type)
- `HookMessage` (type)
- `HookOutcome` (type)
- `ToolHook` (type)

### @cubicecho/agent-mcp-pool/servers

Questions about server rows that need neither a connection nor Node — for the form that edits one.

Importable in a browser as `@cubicecho/agent-mcp-pool/servers`: nothing here, and nothing it imports, reaches for a `node:` module or the SDK at runtime. Each UI that saved rows kept its own copy of these because the package's only entry spawned children.

- `sameConnection` — Whether two rows describe the same live connection.
- `serversWith` — The connected servers that offer a capability — the filter every host wrote for itself.
- `McpServersJsonOptions` (type) — What `fromMcpServersJson` needs besides the JSON.
- `fromMcpServersJson` — Rows from the `mcpServers` JSON that Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and most server READMEs describe a server with.
- `validateServerConfig` — What is wrong with a row, for the form that saves it — before `sync()` is handed it.
- `HttpServerConfig` (type)
- `McpServerConfig` (type)
- `McpServerState` (type)
- `ServerCapabilities` (type)
- `StdioServerConfig` (type)

### @cubicecho/agent-mcp-pool/testing

Test helpers: an MCP server that runs in-process, and a pool wired to reach it without a child.

Every consumer's suite used to declare its own `makePool()` and its own stdio fixture, and every test of the pool itself spawned a process it was not about. Imported from `@cubicecho/agent-mcp-pool/testing`; nothing here is loaded by the main entry.

- `ECHO_TOOLS` — The echo server's tools: `ping`, `echo`, `add`, and a `read` that carries annotations, a title and an output schema, so a test can see metadata go through.
- `EchoServerOptions` (type) — What `echoServer` takes.
- `echoServer` — An MCP server whose tools answer with what they were asked, for a pool to connect to.
- `ConnectableServer` (type) — Anything that connects to a transport the way an SDK `Server` or `McpServer` does.
- `memoryTransport` — A transport factory that reaches in-process servers by name, for `McpPoolOptions.createTransport`.
- `memoryRow` — A row for an in-memory server.
- `makePool` — A pool for a test: silent, named, and reaching in-process servers where `servers` is given.
- `echoServerPath` — The path of a stdio script that serves `echoServer()`, for a test that wants a real child.
